about: Textbook values the earth labs' models must give (#70, 2026-11-06). tests/earth_model_checks.gd reads every entry. Each entry names its source and its tolerance. The sun model (experiments/earth_lab/sun_model.gd) has a circular orbit, local solar time and no equation of time, so it matches the almanac within minutes, not seconds.

place.name: Seoul
place.source: Seoul (city hall about 37°34'N 126°58'E); Hutton Island's stand-in place (docs/islands/hutton.md)

tilt.source: IAU obliquity of the ecliptic, J2000.0: 23°26'21" = 23.439°

rotation.source: 초등 과학 6-2 '지구와 달의 운동': 지구는 하루에 한 바퀴 자전한다 (one solar day = 24 h)

noon_altitude.source: 중학교 과학 3 '태양의 남중 고도' = 90° − 위도 + 적위

day_length.source: NOAA Solar Calculator algorithm (Meeus; https://gml.noaa.gov/grad/solcalc/calcdetails.html), computed 2026-11-06 for Seoul 37.5665°N 126.978°E, UTC+9: 06-21 05:11-19:57 (14h46m), 12-22 07:44-17:17 (9h34m), 03-20 06:36-18:43 (12h07m). Sunrise is the sun's centre at -0.833° (refraction and the upper limb), the model's default horizon. Not yet checked against KASI's almanac (astro.kasi.re.kr). The tolerance covers the year-to-year shift of the solstice day and the circular orbit.
day_length.geometric_note: With the geometric horizon (centre at 0°) the solstice days at Seoul come out 8-12 minutes shorter (14 h 36 m, 9 h 24 m): the check below holds the model to that too, so a change of horizon is seen.

upright.source: 초등 과학 6-2 '계절의 변화': 자전축이 기울어지지 않으면 태양의 남중 고도가 일 년 내내 같아 계절이 생기지 않는다

shadow.source: 초등 과학 3-1·5-1 '그림자': 그림자는 해의 반대쪽에 생기고 해가 높을수록 짧다; 북반구에서 한낮의 그림자는 북쪽을 가리킨다. Lengths: 1 m / tan(noon altitude)

sunrise.source: 초등 과학 '해는 동쪽에서 떠서 서쪽으로 진다'; sunrise azimuth cos A = sin(declination) / cos(latitude) at the geometric horizon (spherical astronomy), Seoul about 60° (June) and 120° (December)
